value.rationale: The motivating interval realization problem is qualitative. This theorem gives a natural complete answer at the first differentiable level: exactly which local linear stability rates at every point of a prescribed arbitrary closed attractor are possible, and exactly which repeller rates are compatible across accumulating complementary intervals. It proves independent freedom to set each basin boundary anywhere inside its gap, while ensuring global C1 regularity and a full-measure basin. This distinguishes a rigid accumulation-point multiplier law from flexible isolated-point and separator dynamics. The fact is structural, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerically motivated constant.
